### Q30. Which finding is consistent with a stage 2 pressure injury?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Full-thickness loss obscured by eschar
- **B.** Intact skin with nonblanchable redness only
- **C.** Exposed muscle and bone
- **D.** Partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis and no visible adipose tissue

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis and no visible adipose tissue**

Dermis skin ki epidermis ke neeche wali layer hai. Stage 2 mein partial-thickness loss se viable pink ya red moist dermis dikh sakti hai. Serum-filled blister bhi ho sakta hai. Fat, granulation tissue, slough aur eschar stage 2 mein nahi hone chahiye. Pressure-related cause confirm karo. Moisture dermatitis aur skin tear ko stage 2 label mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Eschar agar full-thickness damage ki depth hide kare toh unstageable injury consider hoti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Intact nonblanchable redness stage 1 ki finding hai.
- **C (Galat):** Exposed muscle ya bone stage 4 ke saath consistent hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Exposed dermis aur visible fat na hona stage 2 ki depth ko describe karta hai, agar wound pressure-related hai.

**Exam clue:** Stage 2 = partial thickness, dermis visible, no fat/slough/eschar.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-3-pressure-injury)

### Q36. A pressure injury exposes tendon and bone at its base. Which stage is consistent?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Stage 4
- **B.** Stage 3 without deeper structure exposure
- **C.** Stage 1
- **D.** Stage 2

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Stage 4**

Tendon muscle ko bone se jodta hai. Pressure injury mein tendon ya bone expose hone ka matlab damage skin se kaafi neeche pahunch chuka hai. Yeh stage 4 ki finding hai. Patient ki perfusion, infection ke signs, pain aur wound extent assess karo aur specialist ko involve karo. Exposed bone se osteomyelitis ka suspicion ho sakta hai, lekin bone exposure akela infection confirm nahi karta.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Stage 4 mein full-thickness tissue loss ke saath tendon ya bone exposed ya palpable ho sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Stage 3 mein tendon ya bone expose nahi hoti, jo yahan present hai.
- **C (Galat):** Stage 1 mein skin intact hoti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Stage 2 mein sirf partial-thickness skin loss hota hai.

**Exam clue:** Exposed/palpable tendon or bone in pressure injury = stage 4.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-3-pressure-injury) · [Reference 2](https://www.msdmanuals.com/professional/dermatologic-disorders/pressure-injury/pressure-injuries)

### Q41. A bedbound patient has intact skin with persistent nonblanchable redness over the sacrum. Which pressure injury stage is consistent?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Stage 2
- **B.** Unstageable
- **C.** Stage 1
- **D.** Stage 3

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Stage 1**

Sacrum spine ke neeche ki bony area hai. Jab patient der tak ek hi position mein rehta hai, pressure aur shear se tissue ka blood supply aur cell function affect ho sakte hain. Agar skin abhi intact hai lekin localized redness pressure release karne par bhi fade nahi hoti, toh stage 1 consider karte hain. Dark skin mein visible redness kam clear ho sakti hai, isliye surrounding skin se color, warmth, firmness aur pain compare karo. Pressure offload karo aur reassess karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Stage 2 mein skin ka partial-thickness loss ya serum-filled blister hota hai, jo is stem mein nahi hai.
- **B (Galat):** Unstageable mein open full-thickness injury ki depth slough ya eschar se hidden hoti hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Intact skin par persistent nonblanchable redness aur pressure history stage 1 ko support karti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Stage 3 mein skin ki poori thickness lost hoti hai aur fat visible ho sakta hai. Yahan skin intact hai.

**Exam clue:** Intact skin + nonblanchable localized redness = stage 1.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-3-pressure-injury) · [Reference 2](https://www.internationalguideline.com/assessment)

### Q120. A pressure injury has full-thickness skin loss with visible adipose tissue but no exposed fascia, muscle, tendon or bone. Which stage fits?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Stage 1
- **B.** Stage 2
- **C.** Stage 3
- **D.** Stage 4

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Stage 3**

Full-thickness skin loss mein epidermis aur dermis dono ki poori thickness damage ho chuki hoti hai. Stage 3 mein subcutaneous adipose tissue yani skin ke neeche ka fat dikh sakta hai. Wound ki depth body site ke hisaab se vary karti hai. Agar fascia, muscle, tendon, ligament, cartilage ya bone exposed ya directly palpable ho, toh stage 4 consider karo. Slough poori depth hide kare toh stage confirm nahi kar sakte.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Stage 1 mein skin intact hoti hai, isliye fat visible nahi hota.
- **B (Galat):** Stage 2 dermis tak limited hota hai aur fat visible nahi hota.
- **C (Sahi):** Visible adipose tissue aur deeper structure exposure na hona stage 3 ke saath consistent hai.
- **D (Galat):** Stage 4 ke liye deeper supporting structure exposed ya directly palpable hona chahiye.

**Exam clue:** Visible fat without exposed deeper structures = stage 3, when depth is assessable.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-3-pressure-injury)

### Q26. A pressure injury base is entirely covered by slough and eschar, preventing confirmation of tissue depth. How should it be classified?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Healed stage 4
- **B.** Unstageable pressure injury
- **C.** Stage 1 by default
- **D.** Stage 2 by default

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Unstageable pressure injury**

Slough dead ya nonviable tissue ka soft moist material ho sakta hai. Eschar usually dry dark necrotic tissue ki layer hoti hai. Jab yeh wound base ko cover karke tissue loss ki actual extent nahi dekhne dete, toh unstageable pressure injury classify karte hain. Sirf staging karne ke liye stable dry heel eschar ya ischemic limb eschar ko remove nahi karna chahiye. Perfusion aur specialist assessment important hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Healed stage 4 kehne ke liye healing history chahiye. Current obscured wound ko healed assume nahi kar sakte.
- **B (Sahi):** Depth obscured hone se stage 3 aur stage 4 ke beech reliable distinction nahi ho sakta, isliye unstageable correct hai.
- **C (Galat):** Stage 1 mein skin intact hoti hai, wound base par necrotic covering nahi hoti.
- **D (Galat):** Stage 2 mein visible dermis hoti hai aur slough ya eschar nahi hota.

**Exam clue:** Unstageable = full-thickness injury whose depth is obscured.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-3-pressure-injury) · [Reference 2](https://www.msdmanuals.com/professional/dermatologic-disorders/pressure-injury/pressure-injuries)

### Q34. A patient has persistent deep maroon discoloration of intact heel skin after prolonged pressure. Which category should be considered?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Stage 2 in every case
- **B.** Skin tear by definition
- **C.** Deep tissue pressure injury
- **D.** Normal blanchable erythema

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Deep tissue pressure injury**

Deep tissue pressure injury mein damage deep tissue mein shuru ho sakta hai, jab pressure aur shear bone ke paas tissues ko affect karte hain. Surface skin intact reh sakti hai, lekin deep red, maroon ya purple nonblanchable discoloration dikh sakti hai. Pressure history, skin temperature, pain aur perfusion assess karo. Vascular ischemia, trauma ya doosre causes ko exclude karo, kyunki color akela diagnosis confirm nahi karta.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Stage 2 mein exposed dermis ya serum-filled blister hota hai, har maroon area stage 2 nahi hota.
- **B (Galat):** Skin tear mechanical trauma se skin layers separate hone ki injury hai. Is stem se skin tear establish nahi hoti.
- **C (Sahi):** Prolonged pressure ke baad persistent maroon change deep tissue pressure injury ka warning pattern hai.
- **D (Galat):** Persistent maroon discoloration normal temporary blanchable redness se different hai.

**Exam clue:** Maroon/purple nonblanchable pressure-related change → consider DTPI.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-3-pressure-injury) · [Reference 2](https://www.internationalguideline.com/assessment)

### Q65. Which intervention directly reduces sustained pressure on the heels in a bedbound patient?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Keep both heels pressed against the mattress
- **B.** Place a hard ring beneath each heel
- **C.** Offload the heels with appropriate support and reassess positioning
- **D.** Massage persistent nonblanchable redness

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Offload the heels with appropriate support and reassess positioning**

Heel ke neeche calcaneus yani heel bone hoti hai aur soft tissue comparatively kam hota hai. Sustained pressure se local tissue damage ho sakta hai. Heel ko bed surface se completely offload karne ke liye appropriate calf support ya assessed heel suspension device use karo. Device fit, skin, circulation aur alignment regularly reassess karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Heel mattress se pressed rahe toh sustained pressure kam nahi hoga.
- **B (Galat):** Hard ring edge par concentrated pressure bana sakti hai aur safe offloading ka substitute nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Appropriate offloading heel aur mattress ka contact pressure kam karti hai. Reassessment se naya pressure point identify hota hai.
- **D (Galat):** Nonblanchable redness massage karne se vulnerable tissue par aur mechanical force pad sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Float the heel safely and check skin/device fit.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.internationalguideline.com/repositioning) · [Reference 2](https://www.internationalguideline.com/assessment)

### Q100. A patient has incontinence, diffuse irregular superficial redness across the buttocks and no clear pressure-point pattern. Which assessment is important?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Apply pressure staging to all dermatitis
- **B.** Assume the skin is normal because moisture is present
- **C.** Classify every area as stage 3 pressure injury
- **D.** Consider moisture-associated skin damage rather than automatically assigning a pressure stage

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Consider moisture-associated skin damage rather than automatically assigning a pressure stage**

Urine aur stool skin barrier ko irritate karte hain aur excessive moisture skin ko fragile bana sakti hai. Incontinence-associated dermatitis aksar diffuse, irregular aur superficial hoti hai. Pressure injury commonly localized pressure ya device contact se related hoti hai. Dono conditions ek saath bhi ho sakti hain. Nurse cause, distribution, depth, moisture aur pressure history assess karke prevention aur skin protection plan banati hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Har dermatitis pressure-related nahi hoti, isliye pressure stages automatically apply nahi karte.
- **B (Galat):** Moisture presence skin ko normal nahi banati. Barrier damage aur discomfort assess karna chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Stage 3 full-thickness pressure injury hoti hai. Diffuse superficial redness se stage 3 prove nahi hota.
- **D (Sahi):** Moisture-associated damage ko differential mein consider karna correct hai. Final classification full assessment par depend karti hai.

**Exam clue:** Pressure injury staging is not used for IAD alone.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-3-pressure-injury) · [Reference 2](https://www.internationalguideline.com/assessment)

### Q28. A clean surgical incision develops separation of wound edges without visible internal organs. Which term is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Maceration only
- **B.** Dehiscence
- **C.** Evisceration
- **D.** Primary intention healing without complication

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Dehiscence**

Dehiscence ka matlab surgically closed wound ke edges ka partial ya complete separation hai. Abdominal incision mein coughing, strain, infection ya poor healing se risk badh sakta hai. Patient ko unnecessary movement se bachao, wound protect karo aur prompt surgical assessment arrange karo. Internal organ protrusion ho toh evisceration emergency consider hoti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Maceration excessive moisture se surrounding skin soft aur weak hone ko kehte hain.
- **B (Sahi):** Wound edges separate hain aur organs protrude nahi kar rahe, isliye dehiscence appropriate term hai.
- **C (Galat):** Evisceration mein internal organs wound ke through protrude karte hain. Stem mein woh finding absent hai.
- **D (Galat):** Normal primary intention mein edges approximate rehti hain. Separation complication hai.

**Exam clue:** Dehiscence = incision opens, evisceration = organs protrude.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593201/) · [Reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/24-4-wound-healing)

</details>

### Q37. A patient at high pressure injury risk is on a pressure-redistributing mattress. Which plan remains appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Place additional firm objects under bony prominences
- **B.** Inspect the skin only at discharge
- **C.** Continue individualized repositioning, skin inspection and other prevention measures
- **D.** Stop all repositioning because the mattress eliminates risk

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Continue individualized repositioning, skin inspection and other prevention measures**

Pressure-redistributing mattress body weight ko larger surface par distribute karke peak pressure kam kar sakti hai. Lekin prolonged loading, shear, moisture aur poor perfusion ka risk poori tarah eliminate nahi hota. Repositioning frequency individual risk, skin response, support surface aur tolerance par depend karti hai. Patient ko reposition karo, pressure points inspect karo aur nutrition/moisture care continue rakho.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Firm objects bony prominence ke neeche focal pressure increase kar sakte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Discharge tak skin inspect na karne se early damage miss ho sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Mattress ke saath repositioning aur skin assessment continue karna best listed plan hai.
- **D (Galat):** Special mattress risk zero nahi karti. Repositioning automatically stop karna unsafe hai.

**Exam clue:** Support surface helps but does not replace individualized repositioning.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.internationalguideline.com/repositioning) · [Reference 2](https://www.internationalguideline.com/assessment)

**Related historical evidence:** [HPSSC Staff Nurse 2021 Series A post code 892 Q9](https://hpgeneralstudies.com/solved-paper-hp-staff-nurse-exam-2021-part-1-hpssc-hamirpur/) directly retrieved third-party report includes a traditional two-hour repositioning option. This is related concept evidence only, not this stem. Current practice individualizes intervals. Official key not authenticated.

### Q40. Which phase of wound healing involves formation of granulation tissue and new blood vessels?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Initial inflammatory phase alone
- **B.** Complete remodeling only
- **C.** Hemostasis alone
- **D.** Proliferative phase

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Proliferative phase**

Wound healing ke overlapping phases mein proliferative phase woh time hai jab fibroblasts collagen-rich matrix banate hain aur angiogenesis yani nayi small blood vessels develop hoti hain. Granulation tissue wound gap fill karta hai aur epithelial cells surface restore karte hain. Healing speed blood supply, nutrition, infection aur other factors se affect hoti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Inflammation mein immune cells debris aur microbes clear karte hain. Granulation formation ka main phase proliferation hai.
- **B (Galat):** Remodeling mein collagen reorganize hota hai aur scar strength gradually improve hoti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Hemostasis mainly initial bleeding stop karne ke liye clot formation karta hai.
- **D (Sahi):** New vessels aur granulation tissue proliferative phase ki characteristic findings hain.

**Exam clue:** Granulation + angiogenesis = proliferation.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/24-4-wound-healing) · [Reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-2-wound-healing-process)

</details>

### Q103. Which scale assesses factors such as sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition and friction or shear?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Apgar score
- **B.** Glasgow Coma Scale
- **C.** Bishop score
- **D.** Braden Scale

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Braden Scale**

Braden Scale patient ke pressure injury risk ko structured way mein assess karti hai. Ismein sensation, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition aur friction/shear ko score karte hain. Total score generally 6 se 23 hota hai, jisme lower score higher risk suggest karta hai. Scale ko clinical assessment aur individualized prevention ke saath use karo, universal cutoff ko blindly apply mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Apgar newborn ki immediate postbirth adaptation assess karta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Glasgow Coma Scale eye, verbal aur motor response se consciousness assess karta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Bishop score cervix ki readiness for labor induction assess karta hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Braden ke six domains stem mein listed hain aur pressure injury risk assessment se match karte hain.

**Exam clue:** Braden = six pressure injury risk domains, lower score generally higher risk.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/24-3-wound-classification) · [Reference 2](https://www.internationalguideline.com/assessment)

### Q36. A wound develops increasing pain, spreading warmth and purulent drainage. What is the most appropriate response?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Massage the surrounding inflamed skin forcefully
- **B.** Assess and escalate for possible wound infection
- **C.** Seal the wound without inspection
- **D.** Assume all drainage indicates normal healing

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Assess and escalate for possible wound infection**

Wound pain ka increase, spreading warmth aur purulent drainage ek possible infection pattern hai. Nurse wound aur surrounding skin inspect karti hai, temperature, pulse, BP aur overall symptoms assess karti hai aur treatment team ko timely inform karti hai. Systemic deterioration ho toh urgent escalation karo. Culture aur antimicrobial treatment clinical indication aur order ke hisaab se hote hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Inflamed skin massage karne se pain aur tissue trauma badh sakta hai, aur infection ka cause treat nahi hota.
- **B (Sahi):** Assessment aur escalation infection ya other complication ko timely identify karne mein help karte hain.
- **C (Galat):** Inspection ke bina wound seal karne se progression aur drainage miss ho sakte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Har drainage normal nahi hoti. Purulence aur increasing pain ko ignore karne se treatment delay ho sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** New pain + spreading warmth + pus = assess for infection and escalate.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593201/) · [Reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/24-4-wound-healing)

### Q63. Which healing method describes a clean incision with edges brought together using sutures?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Tertiary intention without initial closure
- **B.** Healing by pressure necrosis
- **C.** Secondary intention
- **D.** Primary intention

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Primary intention**

Primary intention healing mein wound edges surgically approximate ki jaati hain, jaise clean incision mein sutures ya staples se. Tissue gap small rehne ke kaaran closure comparatively direct hota hai. Nurse edge approximation, drainage aur infection signs check karti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Tertiary intention delayed primary closure hai, jab wound pehle open manage hoti hai aur baad mein close ki jaati hai.
- **B (Galat):** Pressure necrosis tissue injury ka mechanism hai, closure method nahi.
- **C (Galat):** Secondary intention mein wound open rehti hai aur gap granulation aur contraction se fill hota hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Clean incision ke sutured edges primary intention healing describe karte hain.

**Exam clue:** Primary = edges approximated from the start.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/24-4-wound-healing) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593201/)

### Q81. A postoperative abdominal wound opens and bowel becomes visible. What is the priority?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Allow the patient to walk to the treatment room
- **B.** Push the bowel back into the abdomen
- **C.** Activate urgent surgical help and protect exposed tissue with sterile saline-moistened dressing according to protocol
- **D.** Cover the bowel with dry adhesive tape directly

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Activate urgent surgical help and protect exposed tissue with sterile saline-moistened dressing according to protocol**

Evisceration mein abdominal incision open ho jaata hai aur internal organ wound se bahar protrude kar sakta hai. Yeh urgent surgical emergency hai. Patient ke paas raho, urgent help activate karo, ABC aur vitals assess karo. Exposed tissue ko sterile normal saline-moistened dressing se protocol ke mutabik protect karo. Organs ko wapas push mat karo. Patient ko safe position mein rakho aur surgical team ki instructions follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Walking se abdominal strain aur tissue injury ka risk badh sakta hai. Help patient tak bulani chahiye.
- **B (Galat):** Bowel ko manually push back karna unsafe hai aur further trauma ya contamination cause kar sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Urgent surgical escalation aur sterile saline-moistened protection exposed tissue ko drying aur additional injury se bachane mein madad karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Dry adhesive tape exposed bowel se chipak kar tissue damage kar sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Evisceration = call surgical help, protect with sterile saline-moistened dressing, do not replace organs.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593201/) · [Reference 2](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/24-4-wound-healing)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** specific verified mapping pending.

### Q102. Which wound drainage is described as thin and clear to pale yellow?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Sanguineous
- **B.** Purulent
- **C.** Feculent
- **D.** Serous

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Serous**

Serous drainage thin watery fluid hoti hai jo clear ya light straw-yellow dikh sakti hai. Small amount healing ke kuch phases mein normal ho sakta hai. Drainage ka amount, color, odor aur trend wound ke overall assessment ke saath interpret karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Sanguineous drainage blood-dominant red fluid hoti hai, clear straw-colored nahi.
- **B (Galat):** Purulent drainage pus-like, cloudy ya thick ho sakti hai. Infection ke signs assess karne chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Feculent drainage stool-like material ki tarah hoti hai aur possible abnormal bowel communication ki evaluation chahiye.
- **D (Sahi):** Serous drainage thin clear ya pale yellow fluid hoti hai, jo stem se match karti hai.

**Exam clue:** Serous = watery clear/straw, sanguineous = blood.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593201/) · [Reference 2](https://opentextbc.ca/clinicalskills/chapter/wound-assessment/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** specific verified mapping pending.

</details>

## Mock 05

Source: `Chapters/Nursing-Foundations/Mock-Tests/Nursing-Foundations-Mock-05-120.md` (blob `c6caf7eb0ae9cfe1d9886432a34c4fca264da21c`).

### Q24. An open wound is allowed to fill with granulation tissue and contract without immediate edge approximation. Which healing type is this?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Immediate surgical closure
- **B.** Secondary intention
- **C.** Primary intention
- **D.** No healing response

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Secondary intention**

Secondary intention mein wound edges immediately close nahi ki jaati. Wound depth aur gap ko granulation tissue fill karta hai, contraction se area reduce hota hai aur epithelial cells surface cover karte hain. Healing ka duration wound size, perfusion aur infection par depend karta hai. Wound care ka goal healing environment support karna hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Immediate surgical closure secondary intention ke described open healing process se different hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Granulation, contraction aur epithelialization se open tissue gap ka heal hona secondary intention hai.
- **C (Galat):** Primary intention mein edges initially close ki jaati hain, jo stem mein nahi ho raha.
- **D (Galat):** Open wound bhi repair kar sakti hai. Open hona no healing response ka proof nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Secondary = open wound fills and contracts.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/24-4-wound-healing) · [Reference 2](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593201/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** specific verified mapping pending.

</details>

### Q35. Why does excess wound exudate increase the risk of periwound maceration?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Exudate permanently strengthens the epidermal barrier
- **B.** Moisture prevents any tissue damage
- **C.** Exudate eliminates every microorganism
- **D.** Prolonged moisture softens and weakens surrounding skin

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Prolonged moisture softens and weakens surrounding skin**

Periwound skin wound ke aas-paas ki skin hai. Excess exudate yani wound se nikla fluid agar lambe time tak skin ke contact mein rahe, toh skin waterlogged, soft aur fragile ho sakti hai. Isse maceration kehte hain. Suitable absorbent dressing, appropriate change interval aur skin barrier se excess moisture control karo. Wound bed ke liye moist environment aur surrounding skin ki protection alag cheezein hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Excess fluid epidermal barrier ko permanently strong nahi banata. Skin breakdown risk badhta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Controlled moisture healing support kar sakti hai, lekin excess moisture skin damage cause kar sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Exudate microbial growth ko hamesha eliminate nahi karta. Wound cause aur infection assess karni chahiye.
- **D (Sahi):** Prolonged moisture skin barrier ko soften aur weaken karti hai, jo maceration ka mechanism hai.

**Exam clue:** Moist wound bed does not mean soggy periwound skin.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593201/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** specific verified mapping pending.

</details>

### Q47. Which documentation best enables comparison of wound progression over time?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Dressing brand without wound findings
- **B.** Only the phrase wound looks better
- **C.** Consistent measurements, tissue appearance, drainage, surrounding skin and pain findings
- **D.** A different unrecorded measurement technique at every change

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Consistent measurements, tissue appearance, drainage, surrounding skin and pain findings**

Wound progression ko compare karne ke liye same standardized measurement technique use karo. Length, width aur appropriate depth ke saath tissue appearance, exudate, odor where relevant, surrounding skin, pain aur tunneling/undermining agar present ho toh protocol ke hisaab se record karo. Previous assessment se compare karo, taaki healing ya deterioration objectively identify ho sake.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Dressing brand useful detail ho sakti hai, lekin wound findings ko replace nahi kar sakti.
- **B (Galat):** Sirf better likhne se objective size, drainage ya tissue condition ka pata nahi chalta.
- **C (Sahi):** Consistent measurements aur clinical findings together healing trend aur complications evaluate karne mein help karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Har baar unrecorded different technique se dimensions compare karna unreliable ho jaata hai.

**Exam clue:** Use consistent dimensions plus wound bed, drainage, periwound and pain.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK593201/) · [Reference 2](https://opentextbc.ca/clinicalskills/chapter/wound-assessment/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** specific verified mapping pending.

</details>

### Q59. A dry stable heel eschar has no redness, drainage or fluctuation in a patient with poor limb perfusion. What is the safest nursing approach?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Classify it as stage 2 and massage it
- **B.** Soak it continuously to soften it without an assessment
- **C.** Remove the eschar forcefully at bedside
- **D.** Protect and assess perfusion and obtain wound specialist guidance rather than automatically debriding

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Protect and assess perfusion and obtain wound specialist guidance rather than automatically debriding**

Eschar dead tissue ki dry dark covering hai. Stable heel eschar dry, adherent aur intact hoti hai aur surrounding redness, drainage ya fluctuance nahi hoti. Poor limb perfusion yani blood supply kam hone par automatic debridement se wound enlarge ho sakti hai aur healing difficult ho sakti hai. Heel offload aur protect karo, vascular perfusion aur infection signs assess karo, wound/vascular specialist ko involve karo. Agar eschar unstable ho ya infection ke signs develop hon toh urgent reassessment chahiye.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Eschar stage 2 ka feature nahi hai. Massage vulnerable heel tissue ko injure kar sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Bina assessment soaking se stable dry covering soften ho sakti hai aur underlying ischemic tissue expose ho sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Forceful removal se viable tissue damage, larger wound aur infection risk ho sakta hai. Staging ke liye bhi automatic removal nahi karte.
- **D (Sahi):** Protection, perfusion assessment aur specialist guidance is specific stable ischemic heel finding mein appropriate hain.

**Exam clue:** Stable dry heel/ischemic eschar: protect, assess, do not automatically soften or remove.

**Clinical references:** [Reference 1](https://openstax.org/books/medical-surgical-nursing/pages/28-3-pressure-injury) · [Reference 2](https://www.msdmanuals.com/professional/dermatologic-disorders/pressure-injury/pressure-injuries)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** specific verified mapping pending.

</details>

## Existing reported adaptation

Source: `Chapters/Nursing-Foundations/Previous-Year-Questions/Nursing-Foundations-HPSSC-HPRCA-Reported-PYQs.md` (blob `4e7cacd8b9ebd14d73033d9077fcf64d2c6478a2`).

### PYQ3. Which direct measure helps relieve sustained pressure in a bedbound patient at risk of pressure injury?

**Reported exam:** HPSSC Staff Nurse 2021, Series A, Q9

[Question source](https://hpgeneralstudies.com/solved-paper-hp-staff-nurse-exam-2021-part-1-hpssc-hamirpur/)

- **A.** Nutrition alone without pressure relief
- **B.** Moisture control alone without pressure relief
- **C.** Individualized repositioning at an appropriate interval
- **D.** Daily bathing as the only intervention

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Individualized repositioning at an appropriate interval**

Bedbound patient apni position khud change nahi kar paata. Jab body ka weight ek hi bony area par der tak padta hai, toh tissue deform ho sakta hai aur blood supply affect ho sakti hai. Repositioning ka matlab patient ko safely nayi position mein lana hai, taaki pehle loaded pressure points se pressure hat sake. 2026 International Guideline R4–R7 ke mutabik interval patient ki skin response, mobility, clinical condition, comfort aur support surface ke hisaab se individualize karna chahiye. Appropriate pressure redistribution surface par kai at-risk patients ke liye do ya teen ghante ka interval consider ho sakta hai, lekin yeh conditional recommendation hai aur sab par fixed rule nahi hai. Nutrition, moisture management aur skin checks bhi continue karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Nutrition healing aur tissue health support karti hai, lekin nutrition alone se loaded bony point ka pressure directly nahi hatta.
- **B (Galat):** Moisture control skin barrier protect karta hai, lekin prolonged mechanical pressure ko apne aap relieve nahi karta.
- **C (Sahi):** Individualized repositioning loaded area se pressure redistribute karti hai. Isliye given choices mein sustained pressure ko directly reduce karne wala action hai.
- **D (Galat):** Bathing cleanliness maintain karti hai, lekin sirf daily bath se prolonged pressure ka risk address nahi hota.

**Exam clue:** Pressure relief directly by repositioning, interval individualized.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.internationalguideline.com/repositioning).

**Evidence status:** Historical source directly retrieved: HPSSC Staff Nurse 1 August 2021, Series A, post code 892, Q9. The third-party [reported key](https://testbook.com/question-answer/most-effective-way-to-prevent-bed-sore-in-bedridde--697c404f56992687f107db88) gives source option 1 (two-hourly position change). This adaptation uses current individualized guidance and key C. Official original booklet/key not authenticated.

## Existing reported adaptation

Source: `Chapters/Nursing-Foundations/Previous-Year-Questions/Nursing-Foundations-NORCET-Reported-PYQs.md` (blob `9cbaed4df6baaebf9e2168e5b5a0a95e704e17d9`).

### PYQ8. Which pressure injury stage is consistent with partial-thickness skin loss and exposed dermis without visible adipose or deeper structures?

**Reported exam:** NORCET 4, 2023, reported paper transcription

[Question source](https://nextnurse.in/pyq/norcet/norcet-norcet-4)

- **A.** Stage 3
- **B.** Stage 4
- **C.** Stage 2
- **D.** Stage 1

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Stage 2**

Stage 2 pressure injury mein skin ki upper layer ka kuch hissa lose hota hai aur dermis yani epidermis ke neeche ki layer expose ho sakti hai. Wound pink ya red moist dikh sakta hai, ya serum-filled blister ho sakta hai. Is stage mein fat, granulation tissue, slough aur eschar visible nahi hote. Pressure-related cause confirm karna zaroori hai. Moisture-associated dermatitis ya skin tear ko automatically pressure injury stage mat do.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Stage 3 mein poori skin thickness lost hoti hai aur subcutaneous fat dikh sakta hai. Yeh partial-thickness description se match nahi karta.
- **B (Galat):** Stage 4 mein fascia, muscle, tendon, cartilage ya bone jaise deeper structures exposed ya directly palpable ho sakte hain. Stem mein aisa nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Stage 2 ki definition partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis hai, jab visible fat aur deeper structures absent hon aur pressure cause supported ho.
- **D (Galat):** Stage 1 mein skin intact rehti hai aur localized nonblanchable color change hota hai. Dermis exposed nahi hoti.

**Exam clue:** Stage 2: exposed dermis without visible fat, slough or deeper tissue.

**Clinical reference:** [Clinical guidance](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK553107/).
